messages:
aisha_cs: Aperture hit a weird pattern during their onboarding ramp: a few 401s, then a short burst of 429s. Can eng take a quick look?

ben_eng: Can you paste the sanitized logs? 401 -> 429 usually points to key rotation + retry pileup.

aisha_cs: They shared this snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T18:01:12Z] POST /v1/chat 401 x-request-id=ap-001
[2026-03-21T18:01:12Z] worker[3] retrying
[2026-03-21T18:01:13Z] POST /v1/chat 429 x-request-id=ap-002 x-rate-limit-remaining=0
```

rachel_support: Aperture uses a rolling deploy that rotates API keys and spawns many short-lived workers. They confirmed workers cache tokens on start and don't poll for updates.

ben_eng: Hypothesis: revoked token used by subset of workers -> 401s. Their immediate retries (no jitter) across many workers hammer the new token -> short-term 429. Two options: client-side jittered backoff + limit concurrency, or server-side short grace window for new keys.

ops-bot: Incident created: CS-2425 "Aperture onboarding: token rotation -> 401 then 429" assigned to eng-infra.

aisha_cs: Aperture agreed to pause rotation for 20m while we test. I sent them SDK debug snippet to enable logging.

aperture (external): Paused rotation. Running a 5k ramp now, will report in 15m.

ben_eng: Quick mitigation we can recommend: set env REDWOOD_SDK_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 and REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_BASE_MS=400 (with jitter). We'll prototype a control-plane grace of 20s for new keys behind a flag.

rachel_support: Shared code example to Aperture to implement a shared token cache (simple Redis pub/sub).

aperture (external): Ramp done 7 errors ~0.02%. Happy to keep recommended settings until SDK update ships.

ben_eng: I'll open PR to add jitter to default server SDK retries and document token rotation patterns in onboarding guide.

aisha_cs: Thanks team. Updating CS ticket and renewal-risk: low now.
